key_findings.title: Monocular Depth Estimation: A Survey of Deep Learning Methods (2023)
key_findings.summary: Provides a comprehensive taxonomy of CNN‑based, transformer‑based, and hybrid architectures introduced between 2019‑2023. Highlights the shift from encoder‑decoder CNNs to ViT‑based backbones, the rise of self‑supervised photometric losses, and the integration of semantic priors. Benchmarks on KITTI, NYU‑Depth v2, and the newer DDAD dataset are compared, showing transformer models narrowing the gap with supervised methods.

key_findings.title: A Survey on Self‑Supervised Monocular Depth Estimation (2024)
key_findings.source: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
key_findings.summary: Focuses on self‑supervised frameworks that use view synthesis, pose estimation, and multi‑frame consistency. Summarizes advancements in masking strategies, dynamic object handling, and the emergence of depth‑aware motion segmentation modules. Reports that methods like PackNet‑SF (2022) and recent DepthFormer‑SS (2024) achieve <5% RMSE on KITTI when trained without ground‑truth depth.

key_findings.title: Transformers for Monocular Depth: A Review (2024)
key_findings.summary: Analyzes Vision‑Transformer (ViT) and Swin‑Transformer variants for depth prediction. Discusses hierarchical token mixing, multi‑scale feature aggregation, and the use of depth‑aware positional encodings. Shows that models such as DepthFormer (2023) and DPT‑v2 (2024) surpass CNN baselines on outdoor benchmarks while maintaining comparable inference speed on modern GPUs.

key_findings.title: Benchmarking Monocular Depth Estimation on Real‑World Driving Datasets (2025)
key_findings.summary: Introduces the DrivingDepth benchmark (DD), comprising 120k images from diverse weather and illumination conditions. Evaluates 30 recent methods, revealing that domain‑generalization techniques (e.g., style‑aligned pre‑training, curriculum learning) improve cross‑dataset performance by up to 12%. The paper becomes a reference point for future robustness studies.

key_findings.title: Neural Radiance Fields for Single‑View Depth Super‑Resolution (2025)
key_findings.summary: Presents a novel pipeline that refines coarse monocular depth maps using a lightweight NeRF decoder trained on synthetic + real paired data. Demonstrates 30% improvement in depth sharpness on indoor scenes while keeping runtime under 50 ms on an RTX 4090.

key_findings.title: Survey of Benchmark Datasets for Monocular Depth Estimation (2023)
key_findings.summary: Catalogues all public datasets up to 2023, covering indoor (NYU‑Depth v2, ScanNet), outdoor (KITTI, KITTI‑360, Waymo Open), and synthetic (Virtual KITTI, SYNTHIA). Highlights the emergence of multi‑modal datasets (RGB‑LiDAR, event‑camera) that enable cross‑modal learning.

synthesis:
Between 2023 and 2025 the field of monocular depth estimation has undergone three converging transformations. First, architectural research has moved from pure convolutional encoder‑decoder schemes toward Vision‑Transformer backbones and hybrid CNN‑Transformer designs. Transformer‑based models such as DepthFormer, DPT‑v2 and the more recent DepthFormer‑SS achieve state‑of‑the‑art supervised performance while offering better global context handling, which is crucial for challenging outdoor scenes.

Second, the prevailing training paradigm has shifted to self‑supervision. Photometric reconstruction across temporally adjacent frames, combined with explicit pose networks, now dominate new publications. Advanced masking and dynamic‑object handling (e.g., moving object segmentation, depth‑aware motion masks) have mitigated the long‑standing issue of moving objects corrupting view‑synthesis losses. Consequently, self‑supervised approaches rank within a few percentage points of fully supervised baselines on KITTI and even outperform them on novel domains when domain‑generalization tricks (style‑aligned pre‑training, curriculum learning) are applied.

Third, the community has broadened its evaluation beyond the classic KITTI/NYU benchmarks. The DrivingDepth benchmark (2025) introduces diverse weather, night‑time, and sensor‑noise conditions, exposing robustness gaps in many earlier models. These newer datasets, together with the growing availability of multimodal (RGB‑LiDAR, event) recordings, are steering research toward depth estimators that are both accurate and generalizable.

A notable emerging direction is the fusion of monocular depth with neural rendering techniques. By treating a coarse depth map as a scaffold for a lightweight NeRF decoder, researchers have shown significant gains in fine‑grained geometry recovery, especially for indoor scenes with intricate occlusions.

In summary, the 2023‑2025 timeline marks a maturation phase: transformer architectures provide richer representations, self‑supervised learning yields data‑efficient training, and rigorous, diverse benchmarks are driving robustness. Future work is expected to concentrate on (i) unified frameworks that jointly learn depth, pose, and semantics, (ii) lightweight transformer variants for real‑time deployment on edge devices, and (iii) tighter integration with neural rendering to achieve sub‑pixel depth fidelity.
